subject: MAP tether — Acceptance checklist, exit gates & acceptance tests
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria@avaclinic.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP request — trial acceptance baseline and schedule

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to formalize a short mutual action plan (MAP) to run a focused evaluation of Redwood for our scheduling and triage workflows. High level asks: a) what are the acceptance tests we should run? b) what are the clear exit gates so we can sign off quickly? c) who owns each validation task?

Attached is a short discovery doc with our priority use cases and a sample dataset. Goal: 3-week evaluation, decision at the end for pilot vs. no-go. Can Redwood sketch an acceptance checklist and proposed timeline? Also include any required security evidence for procurement.

Best,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Product, Ava Clinic

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria@avaclinic.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request — trial acceptance baseline and schedule

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the clear brief. I sketched a compact acceptance playbook (see below) that we can refine. Key concept: "tether" — we align on a small set of gating signals that, if met, indicate we’re ready to proceed to pilot and procurement.

Proposed Exit Gates (high level):
- Functional correctness: 90%+ pass rate on your labeled triage dataset (primary intents) across 3 consecutive daily runs.
- Latency: P95 token generation < 450ms at target concurrency (25 concurrent users).
- Reliability: 99.5% ingestion-to-first-token availability during 2 business-day smoke window.
- Safety/QA: No high-severity hallucination incidents in the top-100 queries (manual review).
- Security: SOC 2 evidence & customer-specific data handling checklist reviewed and accepted.

Acceptance Tests (examples):
- Distributed smoke: run canonical dataset through API; compare labels and surface confidence buckets.
- Load run: synthetic concurrency to validate P95 SLA and autoscaling behavior.
- Latency profiling: targeted prompt lengths to match production mix.
- Edge-case probes: curated failure prompts to validate guardrails.

Owners (initial):
- Redwood: test harness, load scripts, latency profiling, security artifacts (So oj in lead).
- Ava Clinic: labeled dataset, success thresholds per intent, procurement contact for security signoff (Maria).
- CS (Marissa): coordinate cutover plan and acceptance signoff.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (alignment): finalize MAP and test datasets (3 days).
- Week 1: baseline functional runs + initial smoke.
- Week 2: focused tuning & load tests.
- Week 3: final smoke, signoff meeting; decision on pilot.

I attached a brief acceptance grid (PDF) summarizing gates and pass/fail criteria. If that looks good, Marissa and Ben can add resource-level tasks and we can lock dates.

Thanks — sending this as a working draft.

– Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acceptance_grid_v0.1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Team —

Nice draft, Soojin. A few operational clarifications before we share a finalized MAP with Ava:

1) Data/labeling: Maria — can you confirm the dataset size (sample says ~3k labeled records) and whether we have a subset that represents high-risk paths? We need a 500-case holdout for final validation.

2) Metrics: I'll add an explicit concordance metric (F1) per intent and a disagreement review step for anything between 0.6–0.9 confidence.

3) Logistics: propose we lock the signoff meeting on Fri of Week 3 (UTC-friendly mid-day). Ben — can you prepare a brief procurement checklist to surface standard redlines and expected T&Cs?

If we get dataset and security questionnaire this week, engineering can start smoke tests early next week.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
